issues.title: Traditional namespace declaration used
issues.description: The rule requires C# files to use file-scoped namespace declarations (ending with semicolon without braces), but this file uses traditional namespace declarations with opening and closing braces.

issues.title: Unnecessary re-rendering on every parameter update with same display name
issues.description: The DisplayName component removed the check that prevents re-rendering when the display name hasn't changed (line 50-51). This means that every time SetParametersAsync is called with a changed expression (even if it results in the same display name), the component will trigger a render. This causes performance degradation in scenarios with frequent parameter updates, such as forms with dynamic field expressions, leading to unnecessary DOM updates and potential flickering in the UI.

issues.title: Missing display name caching causes performance degradation
issues.description: The GetDisplayName(MemberInfo) method in ExpressionMemberAccessor no longer uses the _displayNameCache dictionary to cache display names (lines 53-74). Instead, it performs reflection operations (GetCustomAttribute) on every call. Since this method is called frequently during component rendering and the DisplayName component can be used extensively throughout forms, this creates a significant performance bottleneck. The cache was specifically designed to avoid repeated reflection calls, and its removal will cause measurable slowdowns in forms with many DisplayName components.

issues.title: Incomplete cache clearing during hot reload causes stale display names
issues.description: The ClearCache method only clears _memberInfoCache but fails to clear _displayNameCache (line 85). During hot reload scenarios when metadata updates occur, the HotReloadManager triggers ClearCache to ensure fresh metadata is loaded. However, with _displayNameCache not being cleared, the component will continue to display stale display names from cached MemberInfo objects even after the attributes have been modified in code. This breaks the hot reload functionality for DisplayAttribute and DisplayNameAttribute changes, requiring developers to restart the application to see attribute changes take effect.

issues.title: Test method missing required AAA pattern comments
issues.description: The test method 'SupportsLocalizationWithResourceType' violates AGENTS.md Rule 6 which requires all test methods to include explicit '// Arrange', '// Act', and '// Assert' comments. This rule was explicitly defined in the AGENTS.md file added in this same PR. All other test methods in DisplayNameTest.cs correctly follow this pattern with proper AAA comments, but this test method has none of the required comments, making it inconsistent with repository standards and harder to maintain.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #64636 - Blazor supports DisplayName for models
pr.author: unknown

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds a `DisplayName<TValue>` component to the Blazor Web forms package. Given a `For` expression such as `() => model.Prop`, it renders the label text from `[Display(Name)]`, then `[DisplayName]`, then the raw property name. The Web project's `ExpressionMemberAccessor` does the lookup, and the PR also updates the BlazorWeb-CSharp account pages to use the component, adds a BasicTestApp E2E page with localized resources, and adds unit tests.

The core shape is sound and the attribute precedence matches DataAnnotations/MVC conventions. The main problem is a static cache in `ExpressionMemberAccessor` that is keyed on the `Expression` object itself. Razor builds a fresh expression tree on every parent render, so the cache grows without bound and pins the parent component. There are also smaller issues: an unused cache field, silent wording changes in the project templates, a base-class divergence from the PR description, and some weak or unused test scaffolding.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The Expression-keyed static cache is a real memory leak on a common path: any parent component that renders `<DisplayName For="@(() => ...)" />` will add an entry per render and keep the closure alive. That should be fixed before merge. The template copy changes and test gaps are worth fixing in the same pass, but they are less urgent.

architecture.overview:
Today, Blazor's form helpers (`ValidationMessage<TValue>`, `FieldIdentifier`) take a `For` lambda, parse it into a member, and cache per-member data. Those caches are keyed by `(Type, MemberInfo)`, which is bounded by the number of types and members. The new `DisplayName<TValue>` component in `src/Components/Web/src/Forms/DisplayName.cs` follows the same `For` contract. It implements `IComponent` directly, recomputes its text only when the `For` reference changes, and renders the text through `RenderHandle`.

This PR adds `ExpressionMemberAccessor` in `src/Components/Web/src/Forms/ExpressionMemberAccessor.cs` to resolve display text. It caches the `Expression` to `MemberInfo` mapping in a static `ConcurrentDictionary<Expression, MemberInfo>`. Because the Razor-generated lambda is a new object on each parent render, that cache is effectively unbounded and holds references into the parent component. The PR also changes account pages in the BlazorWeb-CSharp project template to use the component.
steps: Entry point: a parent component's Razor markup passes `For="@(() => model.Prop)"` to `DisplayName<TValue>`. This is the same contract `ValidationMessage<TValue>` uses today.

`DisplayName.SetParametersAsync` (DisplayName.cs) calls `parameters.SetParameterProperties`, validates that `For` is set, and compares `For` by reference with `_previousFieldAccessor`. A new lambda on each parent render therefore triggers a recompute.

`ExpressionMemberAccessor.GetDisplayName` (ExpressionMemberAccessor.cs) unwraps the expression to a `MemberInfo`. The PR caches that mapping in `_memberInfoCache`, keyed by the `Expression` instance. This is the new static state and the source of the leak.
Attribute resolution checks `DisplayAttribute.GetName()`, then `DisplayNameAttribute.DisplayName`, then `member.Name`. Hot-reload clears the cache, matching `FieldIdentifier`.

Surrounding changes: `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` adds the public surface, BasicTestApp adds a localized `DisplayNameComponent` page with an E2E test, and the BlazorWeb-CSharp account `.razor` pages replace hard-coded labels with `<DisplayName>`.

findings.title: Static cache keyed on Expression identity leaks memory and pins components
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web/src/Forms/ExpressionMemberAccessor.cs`, remove the static `ConcurrentDictionary<Expression, MemberInfo> _memberInfoCache`. Razor creates a new `Expression` object on each parent render, so an Expression-keyed static cache grows without bound and keeps parent components alive. Compute the `MemberInfo` directly from the expression inside `GetMemberInfo`, keeping the existing Convert-unwrap and the `ArgumentException` for non-member expressions. If caching is still wanted, key it on a bounded value such as `(Type, MemberInfo)` or `MemberInfo`, following the `FieldIdentifier` cache in `src/Components/Forms/src/FieldIdentifier.cs`. Keep the existing hot-reload `ClearCache` wiring consistent with the new cache.

findings.title: Unused _displayNameCache field
findings.body:
`_displayNameCache` is declared but never read or written. `GetDisplayName(MemberInfo)` returns the value directly without consulting it. It is dead state, and it also suggests the caching intent is unclear. Remove it, or use it if caching is actually wanted (keyed on `MemberInfo`, which is bounded).

::code{file="src/Components/Web/src/Forms/ExpressionMemberAccessor.cs" lines="15-16"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web/src/Forms/ExpressionMemberAccessor.cs`, the field `_displayNameCache` (line 16) is never used. Delete it, or if caching the display name per MemberInfo is intended, actually consult it in `GetDisplayName(MemberInfo)`. Coordinate with the leak fix that removes the `Expression`-keyed `_memberInfoCache`.

findings.title: Template label text silently changes for several fields
findings.body:
The template pages were converted from hard-coded labels to `<DisplayName>`, but several visible strings change. Nothing in the PR description mentions these copy changes:

- `Manage/ChangePassword.razor`: `OldPassword` renders as "Current password" (was "Old password"). `ConfirmPassword` renders as "Confirm new password" (was "Confirm password").
- `Register.razor`: "Confirm Password" becomes "Confirm password" (capitalization).

These are user-facing strings in a project template, so they should be either accepted deliberately or the `[Display]` names should be adjusted to keep the original text.

::diff{file="src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/content/BlazorWeb-CSharp/BlazorWebCSharp.1/Components/Account/Pages/Manage/ChangePassword.razor" lines="23-25"}
findings.fixPrompt: In the BlazorWeb-CSharp account templates, the `<DisplayName>` conversion changed visible label text. In `Manage/ChangePassword.razor`, "Old password" became "Current password" and "Confirm password" became "Confirm new password". In `Register.razor`, "Confirm Password" became "Confirm password". Decide whether the new text is desired. If not, adjust the `[Display(Name=...)]` values on the matching `InputModel` properties so the rendered labels match the previous text. If the new text is intended, call it out in the PR description.

findings.title: Unrelated placeholder text edits in ResetPassword template
findings.body:
The ResetPassword template changes the `placeholder` on the password and confirm-password inputs from "Please enter your password." and "Please confirm your password." to "password". This is unrelated to the `DisplayName` feature and makes the change harder to review. The Login.razor password block also loses its original indentation in the diff, which adds noise.

::code{file="src/ProjectTemplates/Web.ProjectTemplates/content/BlazorWeb-CSharp/BlazorWebCSharp.1/Components/Account/Pages/ResetPassword.razor" lines="33-33"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `ResetPassword.razor` in the BlazorWeb-CSharp account templates, revert the `placeholder` attribute changes on the Password and ConfirmPassword inputs back to "Please enter your password." and "Please confirm your password.". Those edits are unrelated to the DisplayName feature. Also restore the original indentation of the Password block in `Login.razor` so the diff only shows the label change.

findings.title: Implementation diverges from the documented ComponentBase base class
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web/src/Forms/DisplayName.cs`, the class `DisplayName<TValue>` implements `IComponent` directly. The PR description and the sibling `ValidationMessage<TValue>` use `ComponentBase`. Either change the base to `ComponentBase` and move the render logic into `BuildRenderTree`, updating `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` to match, or document in the XML summary why `IComponent` is required. Keep the `For` parameter, the `[EditorRequired]` attribute, and the InvalidOperationException for a missing `For`.

findings.title: Test scaffolding is unused and the render lookup is not scoped
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web/test/Forms/DisplayNameTest.cs`, `RenderAndGetOutput` (around line 176) declares an unused `displayLabelComponentFrame` and then takes the first `Text` frame from the whole batch. Find the `DisplayName` component frame, then read the text from its child frames (or the component's rendered batch) so the assertion is tied to that component. Remove the unused variable. Also rename or strengthen `SupportsLocalizationWithResourceType` (around line 159) so it actually goes through a resource lookup, for example with a `ResourceManager`-backed resource instead of a static property.

findings.title: Missing coverage for key branches
findings.body:
The unit tests cover the happy paths but leave several branches that matter for this feature untested:

- A non-member expression such as `() => Compute()` should throw `ArgumentException`. No test checks it.
- A `[Display]` attribute with `Order` or `ShortName` but no `Name` should fall through to `DisplayNameAttribute` or the property name. No test checks it.
- Changing `For` on an existing instance should re-render with the new label. The `_previousFieldAccessor` path is untested.
- The cache-growth problem above is not covered by any test.

Add tests for these cases. The non-member and changed-`For` cases are the most valuable.

::code{file="src/Components/Web/test/Forms/DisplayNameTest.cs" lines="159-172"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Web/test/Forms/DisplayNameTest.cs`, add tests for: (1) a non-member expression such as `() => Compute()` throwing `ArgumentException` from `ExpressionMemberAccessor`; (2) a `[Display]` attribute without `Name` falling back to `DisplayNameAttribute` or the property name; (3) re-rendering with a new `For` value producing the new label. Use the existing `TestRenderer` and `RenderAndGetOutput` helpers, and keep assertions on the rendered text.

findings.title: Attribute precedence matches DataAnnotations and MVC
findings.body:
`ExpressionMemberAccessor.GetDisplayName` checks `DisplayAttribute.GetName()` first, then `DisplayNameAttribute.DisplayName`, then the property name. This matches MVC's `DisplayNameFor` and `DataAnnotations` conventions, so developers who already use `[Display]` see the same result.

Using `GetName()` rather than `.Name` also handles `ResourceType` lookups, which is what makes the localization path work.

findings.title: Public API surface is recorded and hot-reload handled
findings.body:
The PR adds the new public members to `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, so the API analyzer will track them. It also clears the accessor cache on hot-reload deltas through `HotReloadManager.Default.OnDeltaApplied`, following the same pattern as `FieldIdentifier` and `JSComponentInterop`.

The E2E test and BasicTestApp page exercise the attribute cases in a real browser, which is good coverage for the rendering path.
